text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Chancellor Viktor Klima was elected to be the new Social Democrat party leader. He emphasized the party's "no" to a coalition with far-right Freedom Party leader Joerg Haider. He also rejected Austrian membership in the current NATO. Full employment will remain the party's main target.
- Austria's import ban on genetically manipulated corn is likely to be abolished as the European Commission decides not to ban the product.
- Petrol prices have been reduced by 0.1 schillings per litre. The Chamber of Labour still demands a greater price cut.
- Creditanstalt's pre-tax profits were up 31.4 percent to 3.4 billion schillings in 1996.
- Insurer EA-Generali has taken over stakes in regional banks Bank fuer Tirol und Vorarlberg and Bank fuer Kaernten und Steiermark in order to cooperate in the insurance business.
- Machinery supplier Auricon plans to work globally on niche products after just having restructured the group.
- DIY-chain BauMax plans to expand in central Europe as competition in Austria is growing.
- Regional savings bank Tiroler Sparkasse and Swiss insurer Winterthur have founded a joint sales company WT-Invest.
DIE PRESSE
- Klima has declared the party's interest to continue the government coalition with the conservative People's Party at least until the end of the government term in 1999.
- Microchip-Producer AMS made group pre-tax losses of 100.8 million schillings. The company has sold most of its stake in loss-making South African chip maker SAMES.
- Austrian companies have used up a quarter of the possible subsidies by the European Union which the country's regions were granted until 1999.
KURIER

- Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger plans to raise inheritance taxes in a general tax reform planned to start by the year 2000. Capital gains tax should be raised for speculative capital and in return be reduced for capital invested in creating jobs.
- Bank Austria has not yet taken over the stake of Social Democrat publishing company in Austria's central bank as it has not got a seat in the general council.
- Austrian papermaker Nettingsdorfer is the third fastest growing company in the world, a study by international trustee Deloitte & Touche shows.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Chamber of Economy disapproves of the new minimum corporate tax ruling saying it is still against the constitution.
